clue.text: Redress for Engineers on heartless duty

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps

indicators.note: a heartless word loses its middle, so only the outside letters of duty are kept

explanation.surface: A complaint about engineers who are unfeeling at work.
explanation.walkthrough: REME is the British Army's Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers; 'heartless' strips the middle letters UT from the duty word. 'on' places the corps before it in an across answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Redress is a cure or correction for a wrong, as is a fix for a problem.

clue.text: Indicators of dismissals of Hearts and Diamonds

definitions.meaning: in football a referee shows these to send a player off
the two red suits in a pack of playing cards

explanation.surface: Football clubs Hearts and Diamonds having players sent off.
explanation.walkthrough: Hearts (Heart of Midlothian) and Diamonds (Airdrieonians) are Scottish football clubs, which makes the surface read as players being sent off. Here they are the red suits of playing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A referee holds up a scarlet card to send a player off; hearts and diamonds are the scarlet suits in a pack.

clue.text: Prime CID changes to be made at a reasonable cost

indicators.note: changes tells us the letters are altered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: The detectives' department being reorganised cheaply.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is Britain's Criminal Investigation Department. 'changes' rearranges PRIME and CID together.
explanation.definitionFit: Mid-price goods sit in the middle of the cost range, neither cheap nor dear.

clue.text: Deceive daughter and escape artfully

parts.note: to elude is to escape by cleverness

explanation.surface: A girl tricks someone and slips away.
explanation.walkthrough: D (daughter) plus ELUDE; 'and' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To delude someone is to mislead or fool them.

clue.text: Grace, perhaps, follows sad end for outlaw

indicators.note: follows puts the Grace piece after the jumbled end in the answer
sad here is used as a word for 'in a sorry state', so the letters of end are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
Grace Kelly, the film star and Princess of Monaco, is one person named Grace

explanation.surface: A gloomy finish for a fugitive, with a woman called Grace coming after it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sad' is the anagram signal for the following word, and 'follows' puts the film star's surname after it. Ned Kelly was a 19th-century Australian bushranger in armour.
explanation.definitionFit: Ned Kelly was a famous Australian bushranger, a criminal on the run from the law.

clue.text: Aussie Dame wandering back a bit

indicators.note: back means the run of letters is read in reverse
a bit means only a small part of the word wandering is taken

explanation.surface: An Australian lady straying a little way home.
explanation.walkthrough: A bit of 'wANDEring', ANDE, read back. Dame Edna Everage is Barry Humphries' Australian stage character.
explanation.definitionFit: Dame Edna Everage was the famous comic creation from Australia.

clue.text: Requiring sound massage

definitions.note: the clue's noun matches the answer used as a noun, the action of massaging

indicators.note: sound means the word we want is said the same as the clue word

parts.note: needing means requiring

explanation.surface: Someone in need of a good rub-down.
explanation.walkthrough: NEEDING spoken sounds the same as KNEADING; 'sound' is the indicator, not an adjective for 'massage'.
explanation.definitionFit: Working the muscles with the hands is the core of massage.

clue.text: Confined to bed and kept in store

definitions.meaning: ill and resting, unable to get up
put aside for later use, as a ship out of service

explanation.surface: A patient stuck in bed and stored away.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes someone ill and bedridden, and also something stowed away or taken out of use.

clue.text: Approval about travel with daughter. Zounds!

indicators.note: about means the approval word is placed around the other pieces

parts.note: yes is a word of approval
to go is to travel

explanation.surface: Agreeing to a journey with one's daughter, then exclaiming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the approval word round the travel and daughter pieces; 'with' is a link word. 'Zounds!' is an archaic oath, as is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are old-fashioned oaths of surprise, exclamations of amazement.

clue.text: Knotty Ash comedian tames extremely large piece of cake

indicators.note: the comedian tames, or takes in hand, the next piece, so it is placed after him

parts.note: Ken Dodd, the Liverpool comedian, lived in and joked about Knotty Ash

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of large, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A Liverpool comic subduing something enormous and finding it a doddle.
explanation.walkthrough: Knotty Ash is a district of Liverpool made famous by the comedian Ken Dodd. 'extremely' takes the outer letters of 'large', which the comic 'tames' by having them come after him.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of cake is an idiom for a very easy task, and so is a doddle in British slang.

clue.text: Librarian's task includes former partner in fancy dining

indicators.note: includes means the jumbled dining wraps round the other piece
fancy, as in fanciful or elaborate, tells us to rearrange dining

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
an ex is a former spouse or partner

explanation.surface: A librarian whose job involves taking an ex-partner out for a posh meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges the dining letters and 'includes' puts the former partner inside them. 'fancy dining' reads as a posh meal, hiding the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Compiling an index of books and topics is a typical job done in a library.

clue.text: Plasters some of the aubrietia among garden plots

indicators.note: among means the hidden piece goes between the letters of the garden plots

parts.note: flower beds are garden plots

indicators.note: some of the means only part of the plant name is taken

explanation.surface: Putting a little of a rockery plant into the flower beds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some of the' takes the opening letters of 'aubrietia', a trailing rockery plant, and 'among' sets them inside the garden plots.
explanation.definitionFit: To bedaub is to smear or plaster something with a sticky coating.

clue.text: Shortens brigades manoeuvring

indicators.note: manoeuvring, moving troops about, tells us to rearrange the letters

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Army units being moved around and cut down in size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvring' rearranges BRIGADES.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a text is to cut it down, making it briefer.

clue.text: Even heads mourned "Elder" monarch

indicators.note: even tells us to take the letters in the even positions of the following words, the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: Even the leaders grieved for an old king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Even' looks like an adverb ('even the heads mourned') but picks the 2nd, 4th, 6th... letters of HEADSMOURNED: E, D, M, U, N, D.
explanation.definitionFit: The tenth-century English king, a grandson of Alfred, is remembered by the epithet the Elder.

clue.text: ER cryptically — like recent US elections

indicators.note: cryptically tells us the letters ER are to be described in wordplay terms

parts.note: these two letters are the middle of the word for a school or office period

explanation.surface: Something about the Queen linked to American polls.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is the middle of TERM, so the clue reads 'mid term'. US midterm elections fall halfway through a presidential term.
explanation.definitionFit: Midterm elections in the United States are held halfway through a president's four years.

clue.text: Bird will drop head for nothing

definitions.meaning: a waterfowl such as a mallard
to lower the head quickly to avoid a blow
a score of zero runs in cricket

explanation.surface: A bird that will lower its head in exchange for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: the waterbird, the verb for bobbing down, and the cricket term for a batsman out without scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a waterfowl, means to bob down out of the way, and in cricket is a score of zero.

clue.text: Sparkling tirade about backing help

indicators.note: about means the tirade piece goes round the other piece

parts.note: a rant is an angry tirade

indicators.note: backing means the word for help is read backwards

parts.note: aid means help

explanation.surface: An angry speech that sparkles while supporting a good cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns the help word round and 'about' puts the tirade word around it. 'Sparkling tirade' looks like a phrase, but 'Sparkling' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something radiant shines brightly, glowing like light itself.

clue.text: Poach an employee he and Posh hadn't troubled

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

indicators.note: troubled means the letters are stirred up into a new order

parts.note: U is the old British label for upper-class, posh usage
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: He and a posh person never bothered to lure staff from a rival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' rearranges HE, U (posh) and HADNT; 'and' is a link word. U and non-U was a 1950s British label for upper-class versus other speech.
explanation.definitionFit: To headhunt is to recruit a worker from another firm.

clue.text: Was in contact with Jock, say. Sadly, no idea about that

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go around the other piece
sadly, as in badly, tells us to rearrange the letters

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
a jock is a disc jockey, a DJ

explanation.surface: A Scotsman unhappily clueless about something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sadly' rearranges the letters of 'no idea', and 'about' puts them round the disc jockey. 'Jock' suggests a Scotsman, but is short for disc jockey.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that adjoined were next to each other, touching.

clue.text: One leaves grassland with box for mineral

indicators.note: leaves means the one-letter piece departs from the grassland word

parts.note: a field is grassland
I is the Roman numeral one
to spar is to box

explanation.surface: Someone quits the meadow with a crate of minerals.
explanation.walkthrough: FIELD less I (one) is FELD; add SPAR. 'with' and 'for' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Feldspar is a common rock-forming mineral.

clue.text: Washing a patient has to happen by day at spa

parts.note: to be is to exist or take place, to happen
Bath is the English spa city, and a bath is a spa

explanation.surface: A nurse's routine spa treatment for someone in hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: BE (happen), D (day) and BATH, the English spa city, in a row; 'has', 'by' and 'at' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed bath is a wash given to a patient who cannot get out of bed.

clue.text: Choppers' commercials announced

definitions.note: the clue's plural possessive stands for an implement belonging to the class of choppers

indicators.note: announced means the word is spoken, so we want its sound

parts.note: ads are commercials or advertisements

explanation.surface: Helicopters' advertisements broadcast to the public.
explanation.walkthrough: ADS said out loud gives ADZE. 'Choppers' suggests helicopters, but here it means cutting tools.
explanation.definitionFit: An adze is a cutting tool with an arched blade, one of the woodworker's chopping implements.

clue.text: King partly suffered raw deal, being overthrown

indicators.note: being overthrown, as a king might be, means the run is turned upside down in a down clue
partly means only part of the phrase is used

explanation.surface: A monarch who had a bad time and was deposed.
explanation.walkthrough: Part of 'suffereD RAW DEal', DRAWDE, read upwards. 'being overthrown' fits the deposed king too.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward is the name of several English monarchs.

clue.text: The chap had ages for Ivy

parts.note: he refers to a chap
an era is a long period, ages

explanation.surface: A man spending years with a woman named Ivy.
explanation.walkthrough: HE, D (as in he'd) and ERA. 'for' is a link word. Ivy looks like a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Hedera is the botanical genus of the climbing plant.

clue.text: Davies trained as counsel

indicators.note: trained means the letters are taught into a new shape

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A man named Davies qualifying as a barrister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trained' rearranges DAVIES. 'counsel' looks like a lawyer, but here it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To advise someone is to give them guidance.

clue.text: Fears wild adders

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters run free and get rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Being afraid of snakes running loose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges ADDERS.
explanation.definitionFit: To dread something is to be afraid of it, a synonym of fear.

clue.text: Actors Pitt and Harrison in Yorkshire city

parts.note: Brad Pitt is a Hollywood actor
Harrison Ford is a Hollywood actor

explanation.surface: Two Hollywood stars turning up in a northern English city.
explanation.walkthrough: The first names of Brad Pitt and the surname of Harrison Ford, joined. 'and' and 'in' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Bradford is a city in West Yorkshire, in northern England.

clue.text: Model in tabloid causing shock

indicators.note: in means the model goes inside the tabloid

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
the Model T was Ford's famous car, so model gives T

explanation.surface: A model in a newspaper creating a scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: T (the Model T Ford) inside SUN, a British tabloid. 'causing' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun is to daze or astonish.

clue.text: It's sufficient nowadays to correspond

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, labels the current era, so it stands for nowadays
to equate is to make things correspond

explanation.surface: A modern claim that matching up is good enough.
explanation.walkthrough: AD (the present era) plus EQUATE. 'It's' and 'to' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Adequate means enough for the purpose, as sufficient does.

clue.text: Catch some sleep after hoax

indicators.note: after puts the sleep piece behind the hoax piece in the answer

parts.note: to kid someone is to hoax or tease them
a nap is a short sleep

explanation.surface: Grabbing a quick doze once a prank is done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catch some sleep' reads as one phrase, but 'Catch' is the definition, and 'after' puts the sleep piece behind the hoax.
explanation.definitionFit: To kidnap someone is to seize and hold them, to snatch or catch them.

clue.text: Possible lead in to making a phone call?

indicators.note: possible here suggests one possible arrangement of the following letters

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about what might come before ringing someone up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possible' rearranges LEADINTO. The whole clue also reads as a description, since the tone is heard before a call is made.
explanation.definitionFit: The continuous sound heard on a telephone line before dialling signals a call can be placed.

clue.text: Seller from Devon wandering to far end of Exeter

indicators.note: wandering means the letters of Devon roam into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

indicators.note: far end of picks the final letter of Exeter

explanation.surface: A trader travelling from Devon to the far side of Exeter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' rearranges DEVON to VENDO; add the last letter of Exeter, R. Devon is an English county and Exeter its main city.
explanation.definitionFit: A vendor is someone who sells goods.
